title: Feature Request: Provide Data Conversion Tools from APM, Prometheus, and Log Systems to Dataset Format
body:
I would like to request the addition of data conversion tools that can help users transform real-world monitoring data into the RCAEval dataset format. Specifically, tools for converting data from:

- **APM systems** (e.g., Jaeger, Zipkin, SkyWalking)
- **Prometheus** metrics and monitoring data
- **Log systems** (e.g., ELK Stack, Loki, Fluentd)

comments.body:
Thanks for the request. A converter is now on `main` as the `rcaeval-convert` command. It turns exported telemetry into an RCAEval case directory:

| Source | Input | Writes |
|---|---|---|
| Prometheus | named PromQL range queries, pulled from the server | `metrics.csv` |
| Jaeger, Zipkin, SkyWalking, any OpenTelemetry SDK | OTLP/JSON from the OpenTelemetry Collector's `file` exporter (the Collector has receivers for all three) | `traces.csv` |
| ELK, Loki, Fluentd, any log store | a JSON Lines, JSON or CSV export, with a field mapping (`--field container=labels.container`) | `logs.csv` |
| the files above | `logs.csv`, `traces.csv` and the failure start time | `logts.csv`, `cluster_info.json`, `tracets_err.csv`, `tracets_lat.csv`, `inject_time.txt` |

```bash
rcaeval-convert metrics --prometheus-url http://localhost:9090 --queries docs/examples/prometheus_queries.json \
    --start 2024-01-15T21:12:00Z --end 2024-01-15T21:36:00Z --out case
rcaeval-convert traces otel-traces.jsonl --out case
rcaeval-convert logs loki.jsonl --field container=labels.container --field message=line --out case
rcaeval-convert derive case --inject-time 2024-01-15T21:24:00Z
```

The guide is [docs/CONVERT.md](https://github.com/phamquiluan/RCAEval/blob/main/docs/CONVERT.md). It has the field mappings for Loki, Elasticsearch and Fluentd, and [an example queries file](https://github.com/phamquiluan/RCAEval/blob/main/docs/examples/prometheus_queries.json) with the cAdvisor and Istio queries behind RE2/RE3. Until the next release, install from source with `pip install "RCAEval[convert] @ git+https://github.com/phamquiluan/RCAEval"`.

A few things to know:
- Service names must not contain `_`, and each service needs the same name in every source.
- A converted case has no label. You choose the failure start time (`inject_time.txt`), and to evaluate a method you also need the root cause.
- The derived `logts`/`tracets` files have the same layout as the released ones, but their values aren't identical. The guide explains the differences.

Closing this one. Please open a new issue if your setup's export format isn't covered.
This is now released in [1.12.0](https://github.com/phamquiluan/RCAEval/releases/tag/1.12.0), so you can install it from PyPI with `pip install "RCAEval[convert]"`.

title: fault injection scripts
body:
Hello, I would like to reproduce the different types of anomalies that you inject into Train Ticket to compare a RCA method based on Kubernetes events and use the results you present in “RCAEval: A Benchmark for Root Cause Analysis of Microservice Systems with Telemetry Data” as a baseline. Unfortunately, metrics or traces are not sufficient; I need to collect Kubernetes events during the issue. 
Are the scripts used to inject faults when generating your dataset available as open source, and if so, where can I find them?

comments.body:
Hi @phamquiluan. In line with @nj-apps request above, I wish I could reproduce your RCAEval paper experiments (which is nice, btw) with more grounding.

For example, in your paper you are referring to "*we use traffic control*" (§3.2) but without explicitly saying how or within which data range. And same for resource faults and code-level faults. So, could you please elaborate on the evaluation process and tools?

Best regards.
